openUiAnatomy: no published Open UI button anatomy — single-part component, union of salt-ds Button, shadcn button, M3 filled/outlined/text/elevated/filled-tonal button family

behavior.pattern: APG button pattern: Enter/Space activates; aria-pressed for toggle buttons (out of scope here — see toggle component); aria-expanded+aria-haspopup when triggering a menu/dialog
behavior.chassis: skeleton/button.tsx — written from the APG spec; inherits from no design system

rows.note: Salt: 5 sentiments (neutral/accented/negative/positive/caution) via the actionable characteristic. shadcn: default/destructive (only 2 — no positive/caution equivalent, a real coverage gap). M3: primary/secondary/tertiary/error color roles.

Salt: solid/bordered/transparent/loading (4 appearances × 5 sentiments = 20 combinations, all through --salt-actionable-*). shadcn: default/outline/secondary/ghost/link. M3: filled/outlined/text/elevated/filled-tonal (5 real components, not variants of one).
aria-expanded+aria-haspopup=menu/dialog forces the active visual state even when not pressed (Salt Button.css, shadcn/M3 equivalent convention) — identical across systems

Salt has a dedicated 'loading' appearance, already listed in prop.emphasis (cursor:progress, text/bg collapse to one color, spinner overlays). shadcn/M3 have no built-in loading variant — composed by the consumer (disabled + spinner child), a declared capability gap
shadcn has no distinct :active rule in source — hover and active share one treatment, a genuine cross-system difference, not an oversight

the outline/bordered emphasis, neutral tone — one representative non-default axis cell to prove the pattern generalizes; full 20-combination Salt grid documented in provenance, not fully enumerated as separate rows (scope decision, same as Calendar's locale row)

REAL DEFECT, FOUND BY check-structure.py gate A months after this component was first validated, FIXED HERE (see BUTTON-MATRIX.md finding 1 and CLAUDE.md's Known-open work). Salt's own `--secondary-bg-hover` slot was defined in both modes and cited in provenance from the start but never referenced by any row — a bordered Salt button had no hover response at all. The missing row alone would not have been enough: `style.root.background@secondary`'s selector (3 attribute selectors) and the generic `style.root.background@hover`'s selector (`:hover:not(:disabled)` on the bare slot) land at comparable specificity, and @secondary is emitted LATER, so a naive `@hover`-only fix would still lose to the resting @secondary rule on a bordered button. This row's selector is the UNION of both — the secondary axis's attribute selectors AND :hover:not(:disabled) together — giving it strictly higher specificity than either alone, and it is emitted after @secondary per rule 5 (state rows after axis rows). shadcn: re-checked while fixing this — button.tsx's own outline variant class string carries `hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground` INDEPENDENTLY of the generic `hover:bg-primary/90` (which only applies to the DEFAULT variant's own class branch, so shadcn was never actually at risk of the Salt-style cascade collision; each variant is a separate literal class string, not layered rules), but the accent-tinted hover was never captured by any row either — the SAME `--accent` token ghost's own hover row already resolves via `ghost-hover-bg` (`hover:bg-accent`, dark: `bg-accent/50`), reused here rather than re-derived. M3: `_md-comp-outlined-button.scss`'s `hover-state-layer-color` is `primary` (== `--action-bg`), composited over the outlined button's own TRANSPARENT container — a different formula from the generic hover row's `action-fg`-over-`action-bg` mix, which assumes the filled/solid button's own opaque background as the base and would have been the wrong colour even if specificity had not been an issue.
